operation.name: FMULCSf_m
operation.code: // instruction behaves as if all exceptions are masked
let rc := if (context.evex_b == 0b1) and (mod == 0b11) then context.evex_LLRC else MXCSR.RC;
// Computes op1 * conj(op2) for conjugate, op1 * op2 for non-conjugate.
// op1_* is placed first in all multiplications and FMAs so that op1 (the register
// source) has higher NaN priority than op2 (the memory/second-register source).
// When both arguments to a MUL/FMA are NaN, the first arg wins.
// The sign for conjugation is expressed via is_negate on the second arg (op2_imag),
// so that NaN sign of op2_imag is also preserved (negating y doesn't flip its NaN sign
// because FP::FMA's NaN priority check uses the pre-negate value uyy).
let (tmp_real, exceptions1) := FP::Arithmetic(FP_MUL, op1_real, op2_real, False, rounding_mode, flush_subnormals, mask_underflow);
let (tmp_imag, exceptions2) := FP::Arithmetic(FP_MUL, op1_imag, op2_real, False, rounding_mode, flush_subnormals, mask_underflow);
// DAZ is not applied to the sub-operation inputs; hardware computes full exceptions
// from the architectural inputs. Intermediates (tmp_real, tmp_imag) also skip DAZ
// because they are not architectural inputs.
let (r_real, exceptions3) := FP::FMA(op1_imag, op2_imag, tmp_real, False, rounding_mode, flush_subnormals, False, not True);
let (r_imag, exceptions4) := FP::FMA(op1_real, op2_imag, tmp_imag, False, rounding_mode, flush_subnormals, False, True);
let exceptions := exceptions1 or exceptions2 or exceptions3 or exceptions4;
let reported_exceptions := if suppress_all_exceptions then Zero(6) else exceptions;

If EVEX.z == 0b0, the previous value of the result is read into `old` and the masking variant of the operation is used; if EVEX.z == 0b1, the zeroing variant of the operation is used.
